utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. What I was saying a while ago was that I don't know if it's the same thing on all screens, but on my screen at least, it seems that there is a gap between page 48 and page 49. I infer it from the timing, from the time. I don't know if it's specific to my own screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't know whether -- you say page 48 to page 49.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're talking now about half an hour ago or even more. I'm afraid that we can't solve that now immediately but if Madam Registrar would please write down a note that we have to check and we have to see whether there's not a gap like usual for translation purposes in French. But we'll check that, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. Any other -- so I come back now to my suggestion that we would just provisionally accept the authenticity of these documents with full opportunity for the Defence to come back to that later because they have to some extent been surprised by the exact numbers at this moment. Do you agree? Ms. Pilipovic, you agree?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. When you gave me the floor, I wanted to state one very important fact, among other things. The Defence and the Prosecution, before the filing of the pre-trial brief, were required to discuss the authenticity of documents discovered to the Defence and vice versa. We are now placed in a situation where due to omissions made before the trial, the Defence is now in a disadvantageous position because I am now supposed, midway through the proceedings, to check whether I have these documents at all. Therefore, I would appreciate it very much if my colleagues from the Prosecution intend to introduce documents, to avoid wasting time, the Court's time, they should present them to the Defence and discuss their authenticity prior to their introduction in the courtroom so that we have a ready position on the documents that my learned friends intend to introduce in the courtroom. As for these particular documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Sorry to interrupt you. We are spending a lot of time on identification of documents which perhaps in the presentation have not been well prepared in the sense that the exact numbers have been indicated before. Would you have the possibility to check this this afternoon with the Prosecution - I think it takes just 20 minutes or perhaps half an hour - and that we come back to it later. Of course, one of the reasons they have been introduced now, I think, is because Dr. Nakas is there. But perhaps before Dr. Nakas travels back to his home country, perhaps there would be an opportunity to put out of court whatever questions necessary to solve the problem. I would like to have, if possible, a compromise between the parties on the authenticity of these documents upon resuming.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I'm advised that in fact the exact batch as handed to Dr. Nakas in court today was an identical batch handed to the Defence on Wednesday evening, last Wednesday. So there shouldn't be any difference between the two as of today. As I have said earlier, it is an issue simply of authentication. Clearly, my learned friends will at any time be able to deal with the contents in a future or an appropriate date when they apply to give an individual's -- I'm sure we can resolve this satisfactorily in the break between the proceedings. And if Your Honour is prepared to accept, as it were, a provisional tender or identification at this stage, that might help us resolve the issue very easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think provisionally we will then accept them as authentic and of course the Defence can come back to that if there's any reason for that. If these bundle of documents have been handed over last Wednesday to the Defence with the clear indication that they would be used today in Court, but I'm not going to enter into any yes and no games at this moment on this issue. So you may proceed. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Those were my questions in relation to the authentication. I invited you to accept the documents, and you have now ruled on that, and I have concluded in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaxill. Do we have, Madam Registrar, for the provisional admission of these documents into evidence the numbers we need? The documents in the bundles, and as far as I can see, I have -- perhaps you'll read them, Madam Registrar, before they are provisionally entered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Blaxill, you may proceed with your examination-in-chief or was this --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: I had concluded. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Ms. Pilipovic, do you want to cross-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Nakas, good morning.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: To the investigators of the Tribunal, you gave a statement on the 10th of November, 1995, one statement. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes. I can't remember the exact date. I gave several statements, but I really cannot remember the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I'll remind you because the Defence has these documents. It's on the 10th November, 1995. Then from the 10th to the 12th of December, 1995, then the 26th of September, year 2001, and that was an interview with my colleagues from the Prosecution. And on the 6th of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter missed the month of this year.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: I think that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you left the hospital on the 10th of April?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know the exact date?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: It was the 8th of April, 1992, in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You have the rank of lieutenant-colonel?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I was a lieutenant-colonel in the JNA until the 8th of April when I signed the request for demobilisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you signed or applied for demobilisation?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: When I was leaving the hospital, I was offered -- that is, proffered a document. I can't remember the text, but it was a statement to the effect that I, Bakir Nakas, was leaving the Yugoslav People's Army on the 8th of April, 1992, and that document was supposed to be forwarded for further processing.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Did you personally make an application, or were you just given a document to sign?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: I was just given that document by the personnel officer and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: And that was on the 8th of April?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the Defence should like to present to this witness one document. If the witness could identify it and read it, because the Defence intends to tender it into evidence. If you would bear with me for a moment while I find it. I will continue putting my questions to the witness since I have been snowed under this medical documentation. That is Document D9. I prepared this document in seven copies, actually, but I can't see it now. It was filed right here. With your leave, I will come back to -- here, here, it is. I apologise for the delay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, first of all, I hear that your next number is D8 instead of D9. It has been pre-numbered D9. And I also understand that the interpreters' booth has not got a copy before this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence apologises. In the course of the break, I had decided to introduce the document, so I haven't got sufficient copies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So by the end of the break, you could have given copies immediately to the interpreters' booth. But let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: The Prosecution hasn't had sight of this document yet either, Your Honour. So I appreciate at least the opportunity to see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, of course. You haven't got a copy yet. I thought it would be handed out as well. It's a very short document. Mr. Blaxill, would you agree if the witness at least reads this in the original language so that we also can check whether the translation is a reliable translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: Yes, that's a very good proposal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may invite the witness to read the document. If you put it on the ELMO while reading, then the interpreters can see it as well. Could you zoom in a bit. It's difficult to read at this moment. Yes. You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Nakas, does this piece of paper that you have in front of you, if I can call it that, contain the date the 8th of April, 1992?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: 698/1, is that the number for the hospital?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: No. It is the protocol number where this document was entered into the administration books.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Does it state -- does this document state the following, and I'm going to read it out to you: "I hereby request that my active military service cease as of the date the 8th of April, 1992. The reasons for this cessation of the active military service is emotional in character, the destruction of my native town, and the JNA remains cold-blooded, and the -- cold to this happening," and the signature is Dr. Bakir Nakas.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, as the witness has identified the document and confirmed that it is a document signed by him which confirms in answer to my question that he left active military service, the Defence would like to tender this document into evidence under the lettering of D8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are there any other documents you are going to tender into evidence? If so, then we do it all at the end. If not, then we might proceed after Mr. Blaxill has given --

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: It's a brief formal objection. I at this time see no probative value being offered in respect of this document, so I would object to its introduction until such is shown.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please explain the probative value or the relevance of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The relevance of this document, Your Honour, is the following: The witness today, in response to my question of when he left the JNA, said that he left it on the 8th of April, 1992. The Defence would like, with this document, to confirm that the witness signed the document and that he, himself, tabled the request for termination of service and not as the witness said, that he was sent a document to sign saying that termination of service was coming into force. This shows that the witness himself tabled this request for cessation and termination of service, and we shall probably be using this document to indicate the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BLAXILL
utterances.text: As I understand it, in the examination-in-chief, he said that he terminated the service with the JNA. As regards being "sent a document" he said in order to effect this, he was given a document that he signed for that purpose. But as I recall the evidence he has given in chief, that he stated he left the JNA of his own accord. So I don't see there's any conflict as to his credibility on that issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This Chamber will later on decide on the probative value of the document, but it can be admitted at this moment. At least it corroborates the statement of the witness that he left on the 8th of April the JNA. You may proceed, Ms. Pilipovic. I think it still has to be admitted formally in evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit Number D8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have just one practical question. Does the translation get a separate number, D8/1, or they are both under D8?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The original document will be D8. The English translation will be D8.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before the cross-examination resumes, the tender of this document raises an issue under Rule 67 of reciprocal disclosure. It being a document which the Prosecution has not seen before, might I respectfully request, Mr. President, that before we adjourn today, there be an allowance of a few minutes so that I could raise again the issue of reciprocal disclosure in terms of the Defence completing its reciprocal disclosure to the Prosecution? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you want to discuss that at this moment, looking at the clock, there will be no resumption of cross-examination any more because we would then have two things: First of all, I indicated that I would have all the documents marked for identification mentioned so that it was clear what documents had been marked for identification. And if we need another five minutes for discussing reciprocal disclosure, then I am afraid that we have to stop cross-examination here. But before doing so, I would like to ask Ms. Pilipovic how much time her cross-examination would still take.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we shall follow the suggestions of the Trial Chamber to -- but we do think that this would limit us in comparison to our colleagues. But I will need another 45 minutes. We consider we have been placed in an unequal position. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I'll look in the transcript whether this 45 minutes would be more than the examination-in-chief. But one thing is for clear, that cross-examination cannot be concluded today. So for that reason, I would just confer with my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We are not in a position -- and perhaps I direct myself now immediately to the witness. We are not -- it will not be possible today, Dr. Nakas, to conclude the cross-examination which I really would have liked to do, also because it's -- for you, it takes a lot of time returning home and coming back. But unfortunately, we're not able to finish it now. Therefore, I want to thank you at this moment already for having come to us and having answered the questions that have been put to you until now. I think you'll hear from the party who has called you and from the victim and witness unit how we will resume. I think it will be on the 9th of January, but you'll hear about that more in detail. We still have to discuss a few items with the parties, so I would invite you to follow Mr. Usher in leaving this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I should like to thank you, too, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So, then, I would like first if you agree to see whether we can agree -- well, it's not a matter of agreement, as a matter of fact. I'll mention to you all those documents that we have listed now and that this Chamber intends to mark for identification. I'll just read them for you. It goes from MFI 1 up to MFI 10. Madam Registrar, have the parties a copy of this document not yet? I'll just read it very slowly, and if there's any problem, please let me know immediately. MFI 1.1, with the date, and for all the other dates for identification, is -- it's used during the opening statement. It's a map of Sarajevo sniping and shelling incidents. MFI 2, also used during opening statement, would be a photograph of Sarajevo indicating Lukavica barracks, orthodox church, shelling incident 1, sniping incident 6. The third would be MFI 3, used during opening statement, photograph of Sarajevo indicating Grbavica, assembly building, Makala market, Spikasja Stenje [phoen], also called sharp stone. The fourth would be - and you will get copies, of course, of this list - MFI 4, introduced during the opening statement of the Prosecution, map of sniping incident. Number 6: MFI 5, also used during opening statement, would be enlarged photograph of the Brnje Reva [phoen]. MFI 6, black and white Sarajevo Romanija Corps, VRS organisational chart. MFI 7, enlarged colour Sarajevo Romanija Corps, VRS organisational chart. MFI 8 would be videotape containing various clips. MI 9, colour map of Sarajevo. And that's not used during the opening statement but during the examination of Mustafa Kovac. MFI 10 would then, finally, be a videoclip taken from MFI 8 concerning the French state hospital which has been used during the examination of Dr. Milan Mandilovic. That's the list I've got until now. I would -- unless there's any objection, I would also mark them for identification. And I will give the opportunity - because this list is new to you as well - it will be provided to you. And if there's any reason to come back to it, we will be glad to hear in January. Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President, in relation to the titles of those items marked for identification, 6 and 7 refers to broadly the charts of the VRS. It would be more accurately to describe them as charts of the SRK rather than the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before finally marking them for identification, I suggest that, since I do not hear any objection from the Defence, that it Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. will be SRK organisational chart both for MFI 6 and MFI 7. Any other comment to make on this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, we don't have the document here, Mr. President. So all we can do is accept your decision, the wisdom of your decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As I indicated, you have an opportunity if later on -- that's the reason why I did read it slowly instead of speedily. Then these documents, MFI 1 up until MFI 10 are marked for identification. There was one other occasion, and I know that we have to leave this courtroom very soon. The last issue we still have to discuss, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Mr. President. During the course of the last six days, the Defence has sought to tender a number of documents. This is a reciprocal disclosure trial. Under Rule 67, the Defence is obliged to make available to the Prosecution a number of items including those items which it intends to use as evidence at the trial. At the status conference, during the status conference last week, I informed the Trial Chamber that the Defence has informed me that it has not completed reciprocal disclosure to the Prosecution. And at the time I expressed a degree of understanding at their plight because it's fair to say that both sides have had difficulties in meeting its respective disclosure obligations. However, the first that the Prosecution has seen of the items which the Defence has sought to tender during the week and today has been during the evidence itself. Mr. President, there are two issues which arise briefly. Firstly, I'd appreciate it if we could have copies of what they intend to tender before the witness is called, in other words, they be subject to the same requirements which were imposed upon us. And secondly, as to the nature of the document we saw today, it would seem to have come from a file, a military file, of the successor of the JNA which in the Prosecution case was the SRK. Indeed, thousands of documents which the Defence has so far made available to us would seem to have come from the SRK archive. I am most anxious that the Defence completes its obligation of making available to us that material, the SRK archive material. I can inform you, Mr. President, that as you would expect, the Prosecution has taken steps to obtain that material through the relevant authorities, and we have been informed that the archive does not exist any more. I wish to inform the Trial Chamber that in view of what we have received from the Defence, including the document today, it seems appropriate to me that we should seek to take further steps in relation to clarifying just whether the archive does exist. I anticipate that there will be a motion filed in due course. But in the meantime, I would be grateful if the Defence could be obliged by you, Mr. President, to inform by the Prosecution, say by correspondence, within seven days it will complete its responsibilities of reciprocal disclosure. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I'll give you one minute to respond because this courtroom has to be used in ten minutes in other case.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. I shall try and be brief. After having been engaged in this case, the Defence invested considerable effort in gathering relevant documents for the Defence of General Galic. On several occasions, I told my colleagues at meetings and I explained that my investigators on my team were finding and unclosing documents all over the territory of the present Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republika Srpska, in view of the fact that the archive of the Sarajevo Romanija corps was disbanded and that archives do not exist. In specific terms, the document which the Defence sent to my learned colleagues is a document which does not belong to the archive of the Sarajevo Romanija corps, but is linked to personal documents which existed in the SSNO. It is an organisation which takes care of the personal problems of the former soldiers of the JNA. The SSNO, federal secretariat for national Defence, that is. I shall do my best to engage my team and to have them inform my learned colleagues and the Trial Chamber within the space of a month, I hope, when the Defence will be in a position to disclose all the documents which the investigators, if they are able to collect, send me as the lead counsel. I will then send them on to my learned colleagues as I have done thus far. That's what I can say at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Since the source of this document has at least by now been indicated by the Defence, I expect that you use the time -- of course, I can't say anything. This Chamber can't say anything about any other archives, whether they do exist or not. But I again urge parties to sit together and to see how they can inform each other properly so that we can proceed with this trial. Because I am not a bit worried, but I am very much worried about the exchange of documents until now. So I urge the parties to organise this better. And you have approximately four weeks to work on it but take a few days off as well. I am just looking to my colleagues. Then we will adjourn the case until the 9th of January. I have not received yet my schedule, so I don't know whether -- Madam Registrar is correcting me. It is for sure that we will resume on the 9th, but at what hour depends on the court calendar which will be published, as far as I understand, somewhere in the middle of next week. I will check that both parties will get a copy of it of course, and we will resume at the time indicated on the court calendar for this case, on the 9th of January. I wish you a pleasant holiday, if you go home. And that's all I have to say at this moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 9th day of January, 2002. 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
